meta.title: Chosen gene regions
meta.status: Draft selection, for a biology teacher to review.
meta.coordinates: Positions count letters from the start of the chromosome. startBp is inclusive and starts at 0; endBp is exclusive. The letter at chromosome position p is letters[p - region.startBp].
notes: letters is the region's DNA on the forward strand, read left to right, using A, C, G and T (N marks an unknown letter).

genes lists every protein-coding gene that overlaps the region, in its main version (the transcript GENCODE tags Ensembl canonical). When whollyInRegion is false, some of its positions lie outside the region and have no letters here.

exons and coding are lists of [startBp, endBp] pairs in chromosome order. coding is the part of the exons that codes for the protein, including the stop signal. Exon letters outside coding are untranslated ends.

To read a gene on the "+" strand, join its coding letters left to right. For a gene on the "-" strand, join them, reverse the order, and swap A with T and C with G. Read in threes, the result spells protein and then a stop signal.
protein is the amino acid sequence in one-letter codes, from GENCODE. For every gene wholly in a region it was checked against the letters.
Summaries describe well-established science in plain words. They are not medical advice.

regions.title: Beta-globin: carrying oxygen
regions.summary: HBB carries the instructions for beta-globin, one of the two kinds of chain in adult haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in red blood cells. A change to a single letter in this gene causes sickle cell disease. Its close relative HBD sits next door.

regions.title: Insulin: controlling blood glucose
regions.summary: INS carries the instructions for insulin, the hormone that tells cells to take up glucose from the blood. It is a short gene with three exons.

regions.title: Lactase: digesting milk
regions.summary: LCT carries the instructions for lactase, the enzyme that digests lactose, the sugar in milk. In most mammals the gene switches off after weaning. Many people keep it switched on as adults because of a change in a switch that lies inside the neighbouring gene, MCM6.

regions.title: Amylase: a gene that was copied
regions.summary: AMY1A carries the instructions for salivary amylase, the enzyme in saliva that starts the digestion of starch. The gene has been copied during human evolution. A second copy, AMY1B, sits nearby facing the other way, and people carry different numbers of copies.

regions.title: A bitter taste receptor
regions.summary: TAS2R38 carries the instructions for a bitter taste receptor on the tongue. Different versions of the gene affect whether a person can taste the bitter chemical PTC. The whole gene is one exon.

regions.title: Red and green cone opsins
regions.summary: OPN1LW and OPN1MW carry the instructions for the light-sensitive proteins in the red and green cone cells of the eye. They are near neighbours on the X chromosome and are very alike. Changes here cause most red-green colour blindness.

regions.title: MC1R: pigment and red hair
regions.summary: MC1R carries the instructions for a receptor on pigment cells that helps set the balance between dark pigment and red-yellow pigment. Some versions of this gene are linked to red hair.

regions.title: ABO: blood groups
regions.summary: ABO carries the instructions for an enzyme that adds a sugar to the surface of red blood cells. Different versions of the gene give blood groups A, B and O.

regions.title: ACTN3: fast muscle fibres
regions.summary: ACTN3 carries the instructions for a protein found in fast-twitch muscle fibres. A common version of the gene has an early stop signal, so many people make none of this protein and are healthy.

regions.title: Myostatin: a brake on muscle growth
regions.summary: MSTN carries the instructions for myostatin, a protein that limits muscle growth. Animals with changes that stop this gene working, such as Belgian Blue cattle, grow much larger muscles.

regions.title: SRY: a switch on the Y chromosome
regions.summary: SRY is on the Y chromosome. Its protein switches on other genes that start the development of testes in an embryo. The whole gene is one exon.

regions.title: CFTR: a long gene with many exons
regions.summary: CFTR carries the instructions for a channel that lets chloride ions cross cell membranes. Changes in this gene cause cystic fibrosis. Its exons are spread across a long stretch of DNA, and most of that stretch is introns.

regions.title: HTT: a repeat that can grow
regions.summary: HTT carries the instructions for the huntingtin protein. Near the start of the gene the letters CAG repeat many times. Huntington's disease happens when this run of repeats is too long.

regions.title: TP53: stopping damaged cells
regions.summary: TP53 carries the instructions for p53, a protein that stops damaged cells from dividing. It is the gene most often changed in human cancers.
